findings.title: Equation C.2 uses a potentially degenerate ordinary fixed-space discriminant
findings.claim: delta in C.2 is the determinant on H1(S,rho)^(T=1), while det-prime removes the generalized 1-eigenspace; the expression is asserted to lie in nonzero square classes.
assumptions_verified: Coefficient field Q has characteristic zero.
rho(a1)=-I2 and other generators I2 preserve fiber alternating form J and satisfy the surface relation.
t fixes a1,b1,a2 and maps b2 to b2*a2; inverse of displayed Dehn twist T4.
rho composed with t equals rho; C.1 holds with M=I2.
T has determinant 1 and preserves the actual nondegenerate symmetric Poincare form with determinant 1.

check.type: Exact analytic counterexample and native exact rational arithmetic
check.cocycles: Relation -2*y1=0; coboundaries (-2*w,0,0,0); H1 is represented by (u,v) in Q2+Q2.
check.calculation: N=T-I satisfies N^2=0, rank N=2, im N=ker N. For any T-invariant B, B(Nx,y)=B(x,T^-1 y)-B(x,y)=0 for fixed y. Ordinary fixed Gram is zero; generalized fixed space is all four dimensions with determinant 1. det-prime=1. R=I+N/2 is in SO(B) and R^2=T, so spinor(T)=1.
check.result: Printed RHS is 0, outside Q*/Q*^2; corrected RHS is 1.

counterevidence: B.31 already uses generalized V+; correct local repair is present in source.
B.9.1/B.9.2 distinguish ordinary invariants from generalized eigenspaces; no global notation rescue.
No semisimplicity assumption in C.2; later rho(b1) condition applies only to computational shortcut C.6 and is not used here.
Semisimple-at-one and acyclic cases do not exhibit the discrepancy; no main theorem or nonsquare construction refuted.
findings.core_dependency: C.2 is a determinant reformulation following the spinor-norm lemma. The defect is demonstrated on nonsemisimple 1-primary monodromy; broader core damage was not established.

correction.statement: Replace delta by the discriminant of the generalized 1-eigenspace, and retain ordinary h in the sign.
correction.verification: Exact example gives determinant 1; general reduction from B.31 adds 2^(dim Vminus), a square because dim Vminus is even. No reproof of the full torsion formalism.

independent_acceptance_check.disposition: Retain Minor for equation C.2 as a false local determinant reformulation; no established failure of the main theorems or the later nonsquare example.
independent_acceptance_check.realization: Over Q use rho(a1)=-I2 and the other generator images I2. This is symplectic and has H0=H2=0. The inverse of source Dehn twist T4 sends b2 to b2*a2, preserves the relator and representation, and extends with intertwiner M=I2. Cocycle relation -2*y1=0 and coboundaries (-2*w,0,0,0) give H1=Q2+Q2 with T(u,v)=(u,v+u).
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_check: The second-handle pairing B=[[0,J],[-J,0]] is symmetric, nondegenerate and determinant one. T is determinant-one orthogonal, N=T-I has N^2=0 and rank two, ker N=im N is totally isotropic. Hence ordinary-fixed-space discriminant is zero; the generalized 1-eigenspace is the whole four-dimensional space with discriminant one. The printed C.2 right side is zero, not a nonzero square class. R=I+N/2 is an orthogonal square root of T, independently giving spinor norm one.
independent_acceptance_check.correction: Use the generalized 1-eigenspace for delta while keeping h=dim ker(T-I) ordinary. Source B.31 supplies the correct generalized formula; the extra generalized -1 determinant factor is 2^even and is a square. Replacing h by generalized dimension would change the sign in this example and is not the repair.
